title: Nextcloud
descript: Nextcloud is a self-hosted productivity platform: files and folders with desktop and mobile sync, sharing links, calendars, contacts, notes and a browser-based office. This package runs the official LinuxServer.io Nextcloud image as a non-root container; the application code, configuration and user files live in the application data folder and survive restarts. Create the administrator account in the browser on first visit; SQLite is the default database, so nothing else has to be installed.
important: Requires DockerEngine. Open the app and create the admin account on first visit; user files are stored in the data folder inside DockerAppData/nextclouddocker. SQLite is the default database and no external database or Redis is included, so this package targets home and small-team use. Back up DockerAppData/nextclouddocker before uninstalling with data removal. The page is plain HTTP on the LAN; put a TLS reverse proxy in front before exposing it to the internet.
release_note: 1. First release: Nextcloud 35.0.2 from Docker Hub, running as a non-root container with nginx and PHP-FPM started directly; the code and user data live in the application data folder.

data_notes: `config` holds the Nextcloud code, configuration and app-store data; `data` holds the user files and the SQLite database. Copying both folders is a complete backup.
design_notes: **Non-root, no s6.** The upstream image starts s6-overlay as root and drops to its internal user; this entrypoint bypasses s6 and starts nginx and PHP-FPM directly as uid 1000, with PID, temporary and log paths below `/config` and `/tmp`.

**Code and data in the volumes.** The application code is seeded from `/app/www/src` into `/config/www/nextcloud` on first start (and refreshed when the image version changes); the user data directory is `/data`, so nothing writable lives in the image.
**SQLite by default.** The container needs no external database; the first-run page creates the admin account and the database in `/data`.
**Health check** probes `/status.php`, which answers even before the first-run wizard is completed.
**Fixed image tag, never `:latest`**, Docker Hub only, no `privileged`, no `network_mode: host`, no Docker socket, no `cap_add`.
limitations: SQLite is the only database in this package; there is no external database, Redis, or object storage integration. It is intended for home and small-team use.
The user data directory is `/data`; files are stored in the application data folder, not in a TOS shared folder.
The page is plain HTTP on the LAN and has no TLS. Put a TLS reverse proxy in front before exposing it to the internet.
The first start copies the Nextcloud code (about 830 MB) into the data volume, which takes a few seconds on a local disk and uses that space.
Docker applications cannot be upgraded in place in the App Center: updating means uninstalling and reinstalling, which keeps the data folders.
